label: 01 · Direct ports
description: The first translation: same Claude agents, same workflow intent, explicit API differences.
validation: All 26 ports typecheck under the root strict compiler settings with no relaxations. 61 differential scenarios, six durable-question contracts, two inherited-crash corrections and one interrupted pipeline pass (70 checks). Fixtures do not establish model quality or exhaustive equivalence.
commonChanges: agent(prompt, options) becomes an explicit ctx.claude.object or ctx.claude.text call with a durable ID, followed by result.output. JSON Schemas become Zod schemas; their field descriptions and optional properties are retained.

Shared phase/log helpers use ctx.phase and ctx.log: observations persist with replay-marked stderr output, separate from effect identity. Inspect/list/watch expose saved progress. Unchanged ports retain differential prompt/reply/effort checks; bootstrap and SDLC have explicit question-contract fixtures.

Legacy fan-out helpers use ctx.map with eight concurrent items per group and isolated ID scopes. Bug-hunt uses runtime named maps and ctx.within with semantic leaf IDs instead of the counter allocator. Pipelines still advance each item independently. The runtime independently caps live agents across these nested groups at min(8, max(1, available CPUs - 2)) by default; --max-agents and --provider-limit configure that shared ceiling.

Quiet Choir propagates agent failures and drains started mappers without cancellation by default; the original harness returns null and continues. These ports stop scheduling after a failure and can be explicitly resumed. Completed effects replay by ID, not by an unchanged prefix of agent calls.

Native harness calls record child groups before task input and reap them on every leader exit. Inherited pipes drain for a bounded period; --kill-grace-ms sets the TERM grace. Resume refuses recorded live or unverified orphans, and --resume --kill-orphans stops identity-confirmed survivors before replacement calls. First INT/TERM/HUP drains; a second signal force-kills tracked groups. Escaped sessions and a spawn-to-record gap remain.

Fresh headless calls default to restricted native configuration: Claude skips inherited user/project settings, hooks and MCP; Codex skips user config and execpolicy rules. Native authentication and managed policy remain. Host-session variables are scrubbed before explicit environment edits. The $claude input exposes model, tools, allowedTools, turns, timeout, and per-call USD limit. Defaults here are 40 turns, ten minutes, and $5 per call; tools remain disabled unless explicitly enabled. Historical ports explicitly set strictProfiles:false to preserve this input API. Tools now imply allowedTools unless narrowed; elevated raw tools require write/exec/all launch grants. New workflows should declare named roles, and --profile can raise limits without editing saved input.

Final results omit undefined object properties and turn undefined array elements into null to match JavaScript JSON transport. The final output schema checks JSON compatibility; agent response schemas are specific. The #65 follow-up removes all seven compiler relaxations. Shared explicit option construction omits undefined fields; typed helpers and checked indexing preserve the original orchestration where defined.

Bootstrap and SDLC use durable ask/approve effects with external inbox delivery. A suspended run releases ownership only after active work drains; answer and resume continue the same saved plan and input. SDLC composes spec/implementation inline and binds redo answers to the requesting stage. These six contracts intentionally replace source equality; the original snapshots remain unchanged.

Native output is consumed incrementally, with early session IDs and bounded live agent progress. Private per-attempt transcripts default on; retained parser data, total streams, and transcript files have separate CLI-settable policy caps. Failed attempts retain available usage, rejected response text and validation issues across retries. Result diagnostics use a loose JSON schema so future diagnostic keys do not affect identity; adding the field itself changes older completed agent fingerprints once.

Every recorded agent attempt retains available usage, including failures and interruptions. Pure run summaries count replay once and expose unknown measurements. Optional sticky run cost/attempt gates refuse new admissions, drain active work and permit higher-cap resume; these policies do not alter effect identity. Current Claude totals use modelUsage; Codex costs and its unverified uncached-input partition remain unknown.

The runtime now offers typed inline ctx.workflow frames, bounded profile delegation, recorded child identity, a configurable nesting guard, and schema-bearing definition discovery/registry execution. The reusable cookbook and Batch 02 use ctx.workflow; this historical baseline retains its scoped composition helpers.

Registered harness packages now supply typed clients, strict options and declared revisions without core dispatch edits. Claude/Codex shorthands remain supported. Agent request identity uses harness plus direct durable attempt IDs; new records use kind:agent, harness and revision. Frozen built-in hashes and read-only normalization preserve preceding replay and fork pins. Service helpers use ordinary durable effects with optional inspection metadata and separate local usage totals.

Strictness corrections intentionally replace two inherited TypeErrors: dependency-upgrade admits a failed verifier with no clusters as unstable; api-migration rejects an empty group before that group’s writer. Missing tournament winners now fail explicitly, missing credibility sorts last, and an unreachable refactor fallback is removed. Original snapshots remain unchanged.

apiSnapshot.description: Runtime API inherited from quiet-choir implementation 11718fa8a52549e5fb2bbd3568a267e5d83767f1 (typed harness registry, inline children, durable commands/files, worktrees, questions, settled maps and usage gates). The #65 follow-up changes ports/fixtures and narrowly repairs owned interrupted worktree registrations; this runtime model file is unchanged. Both batches compile under the root strict settings; Batch 01 has 70 baseline fixtures and Batch 02 owns active primitive acceptance with a paired F1–F5 matrix. This model-file hash is provenance for that file, not the entire runtime; tests use the built checkout. Storage format 7 retains replay contract 6.
